# Chart Desk — local chart engine

Local, on-device chart computation. No accounts, no network calls, no analytics —
everything computes from the bundled engines (astronomy-engine ephemeris; Lahiri
ayanamsa; whole-sign houses; mean node for Vedic, true node for Human Design).

Base URL (on the machine): http://127.0.0.1:4700

If you are an agent gathering charts: fetch ONE of the .md endpoints below and you
have everything — no screenshots, no external sites. `atlas.md` is the full pack
(Vedic + Human Design + Matrix). All data also exists as JSON at the same paths
minus `.md`.

## Profiles

GET    /api/profiles                       list (name, slug, category, tags, avatar, birth, order)
POST   /api/profiles                       create — body: { name, category, tags?: [..],
                                           birth: { date:'YYYY-MM-DD', time:'HH:MM'|null,
                                           lat, lon, tz:'Area/City', place },
                                           avatar?: { color, glyph, shape }, notes?, order? }
GET    /api/profiles/:slug                 the stored profile
PATCH  /api/profiles/:slug                 update (same body, partial ok)
DELETE /api/profiles/:slug                 remove (recoverable — moved to data/trash)
GET    /api/categories                     [{key,label,order}] — PUT replaces, POST {label} adds one
GET    /api/dashboard                      desk stats: totals per category, recently added,
                                           lagna/moon/sun/HD-type distributions, running
                                           mahadashas, upcoming MD/AD changes (12 months)
GET    /api/sky                            the sky RIGHT NOW, both zodiacs. vedic: the nine
                                           grahas (Lahiri, mean nodes) with sign, degree,
                                           nakshatra + pada and when each ends; tropical:
                                           Sun…Pluto + North Node. Every body carries its
                                           stay {since, from, until, to} (sign entry/exit to
                                           the minute), retro, speed, and stations
                                           (retroSince/directOn, or nextRetro). "What's
                                           transiting now / when does X change sign" → here.

Profiles live as plain JSON in data/profiles/<slug>.json — agents with filesystem
access may read/write them directly; the server reads fresh from disk each request.

## Per-profile chart data (JSON)

GET /api/profiles/:slug/chart              everything, one JSON (meta, vedic,
                                           nakshatras, hd, matrix, panchanga, jaimini)
GET /api/profiles/:slug/vedic              full Vedic chart (D1–D60 signs, dashas incl.
                                           all antardashas, karakas, arudhas,
                                           ashtakavarga, aspects, yogi, karakamsa, upapada)
GET /api/profiles/:slug/varga?n=9          one varga unpacked as its own chart, with aspects
GET /api/profiles/:slug/nakshatras         per-body nakshatra detail (pada, lords,
                                           deity, purushartha, gana)
GET /api/profiles/:slug/panchanga          vara, tithi, yoga, karana, hora
GET /api/profiles/:slug/human-design       type, strategy, authority, profile, definition,
                                           cross, channels, centers, both activation columns
GET /api/profiles/:slug/matrix             Matrix of Destiny (all points, chains, chakra
                                           table, age ring). Every ring period carries
                                           start/end dates (YYYY-MM-DD); each sector has a
                                           `corner` for its decade point. Each period holds
                                           until the next one opens.
GET /api/profiles/:slug/tropical           tropical positions (no ayanamsa; whole-sign
                                           houses from the tropical ascendant)

## Markdown packs (LLM-first)

GET /api/profiles/:slug/atlas.md           EVERYTHING — the one file to fetch (Vedic + HD + Matrix)
GET /api/profiles/:slug/vedic.md
GET /api/profiles/:slug/human-design.md
GET /api/profiles/:slug/matrix.md
GET /api/profiles/:slug/dashas.md          Vimshottari dasha timeline (MD + AD, with ages)

## Chart drawings (SVG)

GET /api/profiles/:slug/chart.svg?style=north|south&varga=1&outers=0&standalone=1
    Traditional North-Indian diamond / South-Indian square, any implemented varga.
    22 are implemented and all of them draw:
      D1 D2 D3 D4 D5 D6 D7 D8 D9 D10 D11 D12 D16 D20 D24 D27 D30 D45 D60 D81 D108 D144
    D40 is the one astro-seek division NOT implemented — it was left out rather than
    shipped on a guessed rule; ?varga=40 returns 400 "varga D40 not computed".
    The authoritative set is the row labels of the "Varga signs" table in atlas.md,
    which the engine generates by probing what it can actually compute.
GET /api/profiles/:slug/wheel.svg          tropical western wheel (needs birth time)
GET /api/profiles/:slug/hd.svg             Human Design bodygraph
GET /api/profiles/:slug/matrix.svg         Matrix of Destiny octagram
    All SVGs: &standalone=1 for a self-contained light file; the UI offers PNG
    downloads (white or transparent) rendered client-side.

## Bulk import — add many people at once

POST /api/profiles/import      Content-Type: application/json
    Body: { people: [ … ], category?, tags?, onExisting?, dryRun? }
    Each person: { name, date "YYYY-MM-DD", time? "HH:MM", timeUnknown?,
                   place? | (lat + lon + tz), category?, tags?, notes? }

    A place NAME is geocoded here (top hit → lat/lon/tz), so you can hand over
    scraped rows with just "City, Country" and no coordinates. Explicit lat+lon+tz
    win over a place name. No time → noon cast, flagged (same honesty rule).
    - category / tags at the top level are DEFAULTS applied to everyone; a person's
      own category/tags override / merge.
    - onExisting: "skip" (default) or "update" — matched by slug (from the name).
    - dryRun: true returns exactly what WOULD happen (created/updated/skipped/errors)
      WITHOUT writing. Always dry-run first and show the user, then commit.
    Returns { dryRun, created[], updated[], skipped[], errors[] } — each error names
    the person and why (bad date, unresolvable place, …).

    A human can also import by hand: sidebar Import button → paste the table from
    /import-template.md → Preview → Import. Same endpoint underneath. Writes are
    recoverable (every save keeps history; delete goes to data/trash).

    Example:
      curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4700/api/profiles/import \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
          "category": "research", "tags": ["scraped"], "dryRun": true,
          "people": [
            {"name": "Ada Lovelace", "date": "1815-12-10", "time": "18:00", "place": "London, United Kingdom"},
            {"name": "No Time Client", "date": "1988-03-14", "timeUnknown": true, "place": "Berlin, Germany"}
          ]}'

## Bulk export — many people at once

Same cohort filter on all three: category, tag, slugs (comma-separated), and
`where` (placement terms). Omit everything for the whole desk.

GET /api/archive.md?tag=friend&sections=vedic,matrix&vargas=D1,D9,D60
    ONE master .md — the chosen sections for every matching person, each person's
    headings demoted under their name, with a contents list.
    sections: vedic · dashas · human-design · matrix · atlas
    (atlas = the whole pack; it subsumes the others). Default: vedic.

GET /api/research.md?where=moon.nakshatra=Magha&columns=moon.pada,lagna.sign,ak
GET /api/research.csv?category=circle&columns=moon.nakshatra,moon.lord
    ONE ROW per person, plus a count of each distinct value per column. This is the
    shape for pattern work — a nakshatra cohort of full atlases hides what you want.
    columns default: lagna.sign, lagna.nakshatra, moon.sign, moon.nakshatra,
    moon.pada, moon.lord, sun.sign, sun.nakshatra, ak, karakamsa.
    Add &tally=0 to drop the distribution.

FIELD PATHS (used by both `where` and `columns`)
    <body>.sign|nakshatra|pada|lord|house|degree|retro|dignity|combust|vargottama
    lagna.sign, lagna.nakshatra, lagna.pada       (lagna and asc are the same)
    d9.venus.sign — any implemented varga, SIGN ONLY (vargas carry no degree)
    ak amk bk mk pik gk dk pk  — the chara karaka's BODY
    karakamsa                  — the karakamsa sign
    bodies: sun moon mercury venus mars jupiter saturn rahu ketu uranus neptune pluto

    `where` is comma-separated field=value, ANDed, case-insensitive; `|` lists
    alternatives. Empty cohort → 404. Bad term → 400.
      where=moon.lord=Ketu,moon.sign=Leo|Aries|Sagittarius
      where=d9.venus.sign=Pisces,venus.dignity=debilitated

    Rows whose birth time is unknown are marked ⚠ and their hour-sensitive columns
    (ascendant, houses, varga lagnas, pada) are WITHHELD (shown ·) and left out of
    the distribution — only the planets' sign/nakshatra are kept. Divisional columns
    are sign-only: dN.body.nakshatra / .degree return nothing.

## Ad-hoc casting (no profile saved)

GET /api/cast?date=1990-06-15&time=14:30&lat=40.7128&lon=-74.006&tz=America/New_York&place=New+York
GET /api/cast/atlas.md?…                   same views as profiles: /api/cast/<view>
GET /api/cast/chart.svg?…&style=south&varga=9
GET /api/cities?q=lond                     city search (GeoNames, on-device)

Time unknown? Omit `time` (or timeUnknown=1): noon cast, flagged — the Human Design
chart is withheld (hour-sensitive), and house/varga layers carry the caveat. The
system degrades honestly rather than guessing.

## Notes

Computed positions are the input to a reading, not a reading. Where a birth time is
unknown the cast is a noon cast and the hour-sensitive layers are withheld rather
than guessed. Charts are verified against astronomy-engine and published fixtures
(see test/run.mjs).

Engine: astronomy-engine (MIT). Human Design and Matrix of Destiny are third-party
systems; this implements the calculations and is not affiliated with or endorsed by
their originators.
